race.name: RBC GranFondo Whistler
race.tagline: Sea-to-Sky Highway from Vancouver to Whistler — North America's largest and most celebrated gran fondo.

vitals.field_size: Approximately 5,000 riders; the organizer describes the Gran Fondo field as 5,000, while 5,245 riders registered across the 2024 event.
vitals.start_format: Gran Fondo starts at 6:20am from Stanley Park; St. Regis Cup starts 6:00am, Forte 6:05am, Alta Classe 6:10am, and Medio 9:00am from Whistler under the current rules page.
vitals.registration: 2026 registration is open through Race Roster. The Forte is limited to 600 riders and was listed sold out when verified August 15, 2026.
vitals.entry_fee: Current 2026 late-window price: Gran Fondo CA$499 plus local taxes and Race Roster fees; Forte CA$550 plus taxes and fees but listed sold out. Earlier tiers have closed.
vitals.feed_zones: 4 supported rest stops on the 122km Gran Fondo; 5 on the Forte, including the Callaghan stop.
vitals.cutoff_time: Gran Fondo: Alice Lake at 72.5km, Salt Shed at 88km by 12:45pm, and Brandywine at 105km by 2:15pm; finish closes at 4:00pm. The organizer page currently prints the Alice Lake time as 11:50pm, which conflicts with the later cutoffs and finish closure, so riders must confirm that first cutoff in the September 7 rider guide rather than assume am/pm.
route_options: Forte: 146km / 2,712m — adds the Mt. Callaghan challenge (limited to 600 riders)
Gran Fondo: 122km / 2,300m — Stanley Park to Whistler on the Sea-to-Sky corridor
Medio: 55km / 835m — Whistler loop via Callaghan Valley with a neutralized rollout (e-bikes permitted)

climate.description: September is one of Vancouver's driest months. Pre-dawn start 10-14°C, daytime highs 15-21°C. Whistler finish 5-8°C cooler than Vancouver. Variable conditions along the Sea-to-Sky corridor.
challenges: Pre-dawn staging and a 6:20am Gran Fondo start at 10-14°C
Coastal-to-mountain microclimate transitions along Howe Sound
Rain, cool mountain air, or wildfire smoke can alter race-day conditions
Wind factor along exposed Howe Sound coastal section

terrain.primary: Coastal highway with sustained gradual climbing
terrain.surface: Paved Highway 99 and connecting roads; the organizer provides a dedicated event lane on the Sea-to-Sky corridor.
features: Point-to-point from sea level to 650m — gradual sustained climbing, not steep alpine passes
Lions Gate Bridge car-free crossing at dawn
Sea-to-Sky Highway along Howe Sound — one of the world's most scenic coastal mountain highways
Mt. Callaghan extension (Forte only) — the additional late-race mountain challenge before rejoining the Gran Fondo route
Dedicated event lane with regular traffic excluded; emergency vehicles retain priority and the road reopens behind the sweep

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: Prestige 5 confirmed (prestige_5_events list). The standard course is a sustained 122km / 2,300m Sea-to-Sky effort rather than a steep alpine-pass event. Logistics 2 — Vancouver is a major international city, YVR connects to downtown by SkyTrain, and the organizer sells return transport for the point-to-point format. Climate risk 2 — September conditions can shift from cool coastal air to mountain weather. Road surface 1 — the event uses the paved Highway 99 corridor. Value 3 — the current CA$499 late-window fee is expensive, but includes a traffic-free event lane, four supported stops, timing, finish food, and a large finish festival. Cultural impact 2 — a Vancouver 2010 legacy event awarded the cancelled 2020 UCI Gran Fondo World Championships, but without the deep heritage of older European fondos.

key_climbs: The accumulated rollers and sustained rise from Squamish toward Whistler shape the second half of the 122km Gran Fondo.
Forte riders add the Mt. Callaghan extension late in the route before descending and reconnecting with Gran Fondo riders.

course_description.character: A 122km point-to-point ride from Stanley Park in Vancouver to Whistler along the Sea-to-Sky corridor. Riders cross the Lions Gate Bridge, follow Howe Sound, and accumulate 2,300m of climbing before Whistler Village. The organizer provides a dedicated lane with regular traffic excluded, but riders must obey course marshals, yield to emergency vehicles, and understand that the road reopens behind the sweep.
course_description.signature_challenge: Managing 2,300m of accumulated elevation across a long point-to-point course, then holding pace through the late approach to Whistler before the published support cutoffs.
suffering_zones: Squamish to Whistler: accumulated climbing and distance make the second half progressively harder
Howe Sound coastal section in headwind: exposed to crosswinds that can significantly slow progress
Brandywine to Whistler: the final 17km comes after the 105km support cutoff and rewards conservative early pacing

logistics.airport: Vancouver International (YVR), with Canada Line rail service to downtown Vancouver.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Vancouver (start): wide range of hotels, downtown near Stanley Park ideal. Whistler (finish): world-class resort accommodation. Event partners offer discounted rates. Point-to-point format means planning for two locations or using event shuttle.
logistics.transport: Event shuttle buses (purchasable) return riders + bikes from Whistler to Vancouver. Free Concord Pacific Park & Ride in Vancouver. Bag drop to finish line available.
logistics.food: 4 supported rest stops on the Gran Fondo and 5 on the Forte. Finish food and a drink are included at Celebration Plaza in Whistler.

history.origin_story: Founded by Neil McKinnon and Kevin Thomson, who conceived the idea in 2007 of creating a world-class cycling event as part of the Vancouver 2010 Winter Olympics legacy. The inaugural edition on September 11, 2010 drew ~4,000 cyclists along the dramatically improved Sea-to-Sky Highway built for the Olympics at a cost of over CAD $600 million.
notable_moments: 2010: Inaugural edition — ~4,000 riders, billed as Canada's largest mass cycling event
2017: UCI Management Committee awards 2020 Gran Fondo World Championships to Vancouver/Whistler — first time in North America
2018-2019: Voted best Gran Fondo in North America by Gran Fondo Guide
2020: UCI Gran Fondo World Championships cancelled due to COVID-19
2023-2024: Again voted best Gran Fondo in North America
history.reputation: North America's largest and most celebrated gran fondo. Voted best Gran Fondo in North America four times (2018, 2019, 2023, 2024). Awarded the 2020 UCI Gran Fondo World Championships (cancelled due to COVID). PELOTON Magazine called founder Neil McKinnon 'North America's Fondo Founding Father.'

biased_opinion.verdict: The gold standard for North American gran fondos — scenic, well-organized, and genuinely accessible.
biased_opinion.summary: RBC GranFondo Whistler is North America's large-scale answer to the European gran fondo tradition. The Sea-to-Sky corridor is genuinely spectacular, the organization is polished, and the Whistler finish creates a strong post-ride celebration. The standard Gran Fondo is not built around one famous pass, but 122km and 2,300m make it a serious endurance event. The Forte adds the Mt. Callaghan extension for riders wanting a harder late-race mountain test.
strengths: Sea-to-Sky Highway is one of the world's most scenic coastal mountain roads
5,000+ riders — largest gran fondo in North America
Lions Gate Bridge car-free crossing at dawn
Forte option (146km) adds the Mt. Callaghan challenge
weaknesses: A dedicated traffic-free lane is not the same as a whole-highway closure, and the road reopens behind the sweep
The Gran Fondo's challenge is accumulated climbing rather than one marquee alpine pass
The current CA$499 late-window fee plus taxes and platform fees is expensive
Point-to-point logistics require shuttle or overnight in Whistler
biased_opinion.bottom_line: RBC GranFondo Whistler earns T2 through brand prestige, scale, and setting rather than course difficulty. If you want the best North American gran fondo experience on one of the world's most scenic highways, this is it. Just don't expect European mountain passes.

final_verdict.one_liner: Sea-to-Sky Highway from Vancouver to Whistler — North America's largest and most celebrated gran fondo, where the scenery outshines the climbing.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes, if you value a fully produced gran fondo experience and can handle a costly, point-to-point weekend. The Sea-to-Sky setting, dedicated event lane, support, and Whistler finish are the draw. The 146km Forte adds Mt. Callaghan for riders wanting the harder option, but its 600 places were sold out when checked.
final_verdict.alternatives: GFNY NYC (East Coast gran fondo, similar production scale), L'Etape du Tour (if you want closed-road mountain challenge), Gran Fondo Stelvio (if you want real alpine climbing).
